cues.en: And we're going to kick off with a keynote on the future of money. So it really is about looking forward. We're going to have a future stargazing session this morning, and someone who doesn't need a lot of introduction, other than to say he is a world-class expert in his field, has come to South Africa to talk to us. Andreas Antonopoulos, welcome to South Africa, and welcome to the conference. Hi. Good morning, everyone. I am so excited to be here.
cues.zh: 我们将以一场关于货币未来的主旨演讲开场。所以，重点确实是展望未来。今天上午我们会有一个未来畅想环节，而有一位无需过多介绍的人——只需说他是该领域的世界级专家——来到南非与我们交流。Andreas Antonopoulos，欢迎来到南非，欢迎参加本次大会。嗨。大家早上好。能来到这里，我太兴奋了。

cues.en: This conference was called the Bitcoin conference a couple of years ago, and now it's the blockchain conference. Next year it's going to be the DLT technology. After that, it's going to be the database inspired by, but no longer in any way related to, blockchain conference. It's an interesting progression. Let me do a quick poll of the audience. I want to get an idea of your level of experience and familiarity with this space.
cues.zh: 这个大会几年前还叫 Bitcoin 大会，现在成了区块链大会。明年它会变成 DLT 技术大会。再往后，就会变成受区块链启发、但已经和区块链毫无关系的数据库大会。这个演变挺有意思。我先快速问一下观众。我想了解大家对这一领域的经验和熟悉程度。

cues.en: I'm going to go back to the yester years of Bitcoin. How many of you currently own Bitcoin? Fantastic. Those who don't own Bitcoin, how many of you have conducted a transaction or seen a transaction happen in Bitcoin? Great. How many do not own any cryptocurrency of any type? Okay, great. How about people who are involved with Ethereum?
cues.zh: 我要回顾一下 Bitcoin 的早年。你们现在有多少人持有 Bitcoin？太好了。不持有 Bitcoin 的人里，有多少人做过 Bitcoin 交易，或者见过 Bitcoin 交易发生？很好。有多少人没有持有任何类型的加密货币？好，很好。那参与 Ethereum 的人呢？

cues.en: and own Ethereum? Great. Dash. Monero. Zcash. Got some interesting ones. Okay. How many own blockchain? How many have used blockchain in a transaction? Or in any way? Other than the five things I mentioned previously. All right. Okay, so breakdown for you, for those who can't see what the audience is doing. About 60 to 70% have Bitcoin at the moment.
cues.zh: 并且持有 Ethereum 的呢？很好。Dash。Monero。Zcash。有些挺有意思的。好。有多少人拥有区块链？有多少人在交易中使用过区块链？或者以任何方式用过？除了我刚才提到的那五样之外。好。好，我给大家拆解一下，给那些看不到观众在做什么的人。目前大约 60% 到 70% 的人持有 Bitcoin。

cues.en: or have conducted a transaction about 30% or 40% with Ethereum, a smaller minority with Dash, Monero, and Zcash. Nobody owns blockchain. This is interesting. This is exciting. Great. Let's get started. What exactly is going on here? Is this the greatest technological innovation and explosion of innovation since the mobile internet?
cues.zh: 或者大约 30% 到 40% 的人用 Ethereum 进行过交易，更小一部分人用过 Dash、Monero 和 Zcash。没有人拥有区块链。这很有意思。这很令人兴奋。好，我们开始吧。这里到底在发生什么？这是否是自移动互联网以来最伟大的技术创新和创新爆发？

cues.en: or maybe even the internet itself. Or is this the greatest load of hype ever ranged around a technology in the history of technology? Both. And in fact, that's a characteristic of advanced technologies. I often say that where Bitcoin and the other open blockchains are today is approximately where the internet is in 1992.
cues.zh: 或者甚至可能是互联网本身。又或者，这是技术史上围绕一项技术出现的最夸张的炒作？两者都是。事实上，这正是先进技术的一个特征。我常说，Bitcoin 和其他开放区块链今天所处的位置，大约相当于互联网在 1992 年所处的位置。

cues.en: in terms of technology, in terms of infrastructure deployment, in terms of adoption patterns. This technology is approximately where the internet was in 1992, but the hype around blockchain is exactly where the internet was in 1998. You know what comes next. There will be a shakeout. When the waters recede, you can tell who on the beach wasn't wearing a swimsuit.
cues.zh: 就技术而言，就基础设施部署而言，就采用模式而言，这项技术大致相当于1992年的互联网，但围绕区块链的炒作恰恰相当于1998年的互联网。你知道接下来会发生什么。会有一轮洗牌。潮水退去时，你就能看出海滩上谁没穿泳衣。

cues.en: They stand there naked. It's an empty promise. This will happen in the blockchain space. There is a lot, a lot of bullshit being peddled to VCs, to investors, to initial coin offering buyers, to uneducated investors. There's a lot of Ponzi schemes. There's a lot of pyramid schemes. There's a lot of empty promises. There's also
cues.zh: 他们会光着身子站在那里。这是空洞的承诺。区块链领域也会发生这种事。有太多太多的胡扯被兜售给风投、投资者、ICO买家、不明就里的投资者。有很多庞氏骗局。有很多金字塔骗局。有很多空洞的承诺。还有

cues.en: A lot of business as usual disguised as innovation, disguised as disruptive technology. We are at this strange moment where the underlying technology truly is massively disruptive, massively innovative. The amount of research that is happening today in applied cryptography is unprecedented.
cues.zh: 很多老一套的生意，披着创新的外衣，披着颠覆性技术的外衣。我们正处在一个奇怪的时刻：底层技术确实具有巨大的颠覆性、巨大的创新性。如今应用密码学领域的研究之多，前所未有。

cues.en: We are looking at the largest civilian deployment of public key cryptography ever. It turns out that people only protect keys when those keys are attached to value. Nothing teaches someone security fast enough than having their bitcoin on a Windows machine. Holding your own bitcoin very quickly changes your attitude towards information security.
cues.zh: 我们正在见证有史以来最大规模的民用公钥密码学部署。事实证明，只有当密钥与价值挂钩时，人们才会保护密钥。没有什么比把比特币放在 Windows 机器上更能快速教会一个人安全。自己持有比特币，会很快改变你对信息安全的看法。

cues.en: You didn't care about your photos. Some didn't even care about your sexy photos. You didn't care about your location, the fact that everything you do was tracked. You didn't care about posting your entire life on Facebook. You used the same password on 17 different sites.
cues.zh: 你根本不在乎自己的照片。有些人甚至不在乎自己的性感照。你不在乎自己的位置，也不在乎自己的一举一动都被追踪。你不在乎把自己的整个生活发到 Facebook 上。你在 17 个不同网站上用同一个密码。

cues.en: You didn't know what two-factor authentication was and then Bitcoin happened and suddenly you're on a steep learning curve and getting better every day. Now you're telling your friends about two-factor authentication and you're horrified to remember how you used to practice security because storing value has this unique ability to focus your mind on the aspects of security that matters. So this technology is driving this groundswell
cues.zh: 你以前不知道双重认证是什么，后来 Bitcoin 出现了，突然你就进入陡峭的学习曲线，每天都在进步。现在你开始跟朋友讲双重认证，回想起自己过去怎么做安全，你会吓一跳，因为存储价值有一种独特能力，能让你把注意力集中到真正重要的安全环节上。所以这项技术正在推动这股

cues.en: of security awareness. It's driving the most incredible research in applied cryptography we've ever seen. Some of you are probably quite technical. You're involved in computer science. You've seen what's happening here. Nobody thought that we would be doing applied snore signatures. Nobody thought we'd be looking at advanced elliptic curve applications. Nobody thought we'd be doing things like...
cues.zh: 安全意识浪潮。它正在推动我们见过的最不可思议的应用密码学研究。你们中有些人可能很懂技术。你从事计算机科学。你已经看到这里发生的事。没人想到我们会做应用 Schnorr 签名。没人想到我们会研究高级椭圆曲线应用。没人想到我们会做像……

cues.en: ring signatures and range proofs for confidential transactions. The state of anonymity and privacy is advancing rapidly. We are building a whole new world in terms of cryptography. This is applied cryptography on the largest cryptographically secured network the world has ever seen. That is not business as usual. It is highly disruptive. Out of that...
cues.zh: 用于机密交易的环签名和范围证明。匿名性和隐私的状况正在迅速发展。我们正在密码学层面构建一个全新的世界。这是在世界上前所未有的最大密码学安全网络上进行的应用密码学。这不是照常行事。它极具颠覆性。由此……

cues.en: came this fantastic saying. Blockchain is the technology behind Bitcoin, which is incorrect. Blockchain is one of the four foundational technologies behind Bitcoin. It can't stand alone, but that hasn't stopped people from trying to sell it. Blockchain is Bitcoin with a haircut and a suit that you parade in front of your board.
cues.zh: 产生了这句绝妙的话。区块链是比特币背后的技术，这是错误的。区块链是比特币背后的四项基础技术之一。它不能单独成立，但这并没有阻止人们试图推销它。区块链就是理了发、穿上西装、被你拿到董事会面前炫耀的比特币。

cues.en: It's the ability to deliver a sanitized clean comfortable version of blockchain of Bitcoin to people who are too terrified of actually disruptive technology and So you get into this very strange world Where the words no longer mean anything? Can you define blockchain for me? I think a few people in this room could probably define blockchain But the real challenge would be can you define blockchain in such a way?
cues.zh: 就是把比特币的区块链包装成一个净化过、干净又舒适的版本，交给那些太害怕真正颠覆性技术的人，于是你进入一个非常奇怪的世界，词语不再有任何意义？你能给我定义一下区块链吗？我想这个房间里可能有几个人能定义区块链，但真正的挑战是，你能不能用这样一种方式定义区块链？

cues.en: I can't do search and replace with the word database and still make that sentence work Because that's the challenge if what you're doing is a database with signatures It's not interesting. It's boring. What is the essence of Bitcoin? It's not blockchain the essence of Bitcoin is the ability to operate in a decentralized way without having to trust anyone
cues.zh: 我没法把 database 这个词做查找替换后还让那句话成立。因为挑战就在这儿：如果你做的只是一个带签名的数据库，那并不有趣，很无聊。比特币的本质是什么？不是区块链。比特币的本质是能够以去中心化的方式运行，而不必信任任何人。

cues.en: The essence of Bitcoin is to be able to use software to authoritatively, independently, without appeal to authority, verify everything yourself. You don't trust the other nodes you're talking to. You assume they're lying. You don't trust the miners. You don't trust the people creating the transactions. You don't trust anything other than the outcome...
cues.zh: 比特币的本质是，能够用软件权威地、独立地、无需诉诸权威地自行验证一切。你不信任正在通信的其他节点。你假设它们在撒谎。你不信任矿工。你不信任创建交易的人。除了结果，你什么都不信……

cues.en: of your own verification and validation. And through that, you end up trusting in something more important, the network effect. Bitcoin introduced the concept of decentralized security through computation. And this has not yet sunk in. What Bitcoin does is it allows you to replace a security model that is based around concentric circles of access and control with an institution in the center.
cues.zh: 你自己的验证与确认。通过这个过程，你最终会信任更重要的东西——网络效应。比特币引入了通过计算实现去中心化安全的概念。而这一点至今还没有被人们真正理解。比特币所做的是，让你能够用一种全新的安全模型，去取代那种围绕同心圆式的准入与控制、中心是一家机构的安全模型。

cues.en: with a security model that is inside out, open and accessible to everyone. A security model that is based on market forces and game theory. It is the first market-based security model where a series of incentives and punishments ensure that the ultimate result is you can trust the platform itself as a neutral arbiter that is not controlled by anyone.
cues.zh: 换成一种由内而外、对所有人开放且可访问的安全模型。一种基于市场力量和博弈论的安全模型。这是第一个基于市场的安全模型，其中一系列激励与惩罚机制确保最终结果是：你可以信任平台本身，把它当作不受任何人控制的中立仲裁者。

cues.en: Without third parties without intermediaries Bitcoin revolutionizes trust now, it's difficult to have that conversation if you only focus on Bitcoin and Arguably a lot of people have said but it's not just about currency What about the other applications and it's not just about Bitcoin? What about the other? blockchains and So in that sense the term blockchain means something
cues.zh: 没有第三方、没有中介，比特币正在革新信任。现在，如果你只关注比特币，就很难展开那场讨论；而且可以说，很多人都讲过，这不只是货币的问题。其他应用呢？而且不只是比特币，其他区块链呢？所以从这个意义上说，区块链这个词是有含义的

cues.en: But only if you define it very very narrowly I use the qualifier open to talk about open blockchain What I'm interested in is the applications of this technology that enable you to run a decentralized Trustless system that does not rely on anyone as an intermediary of trust because that is The disruption here that is the essence of this technology so that essence
cues.zh: 但前提是你把它定义得非常非常窄。我用“开放”这个限定词来谈开放区块链。我感兴趣的是这项技术的应用，它们让你能运行一个去中心化、无需信任的系统，不依赖任何人作为信任中介，因为那才是这里的颠覆所在，那才是这项技术的本质，所以那个本质

cues.en: is seen in other systems. Ethereum exhibits it for the application of smart contracts, but those smart contracts only work if you don't have to trust anyone to execute the smart contract correctly. You can only trust that that's going to happen if everyone can participate in an open manner and verify each other, if access to the underlying consensus algorithm in mining is open to everyone. Out of these...
cues.zh: 在其他系统中也能看到。以太坊在智能合约的应用中体现了这一点，但只有当你不必信任任何人来正确执行智能合约时，这些智能合约才成立。只有每个人都能以开放的方式参与并相互验证，只有挖矿中对底层共识算法的访问对所有人开放，你才能相信这会发生。在这些……

cues.en: Characteristics come with the power of these blockchain technologies. Open. That is the key word. Borderless. There are no borders. Transnational. This is no longer about nation-states. This is about network-centric trust. Without third parties, the network is the trusted party. Only if you verify everything. Neutral.
cues.zh: 这些特性源自这些区块链技术的能力。开放——这是关键词。无国界——没有边界。跨国——不再关乎民族国家，而是以网络为中心的信任。没有第三方，网络就是可信方。前提是你验证一切。中立。

cues.en: Because it isn't serving the goals of any one organization or institution. It follows the consensus rules neutrally. Everyone follows the consensus rules neutrally. Your transaction, there is no such thing as a good transaction or a bad transaction, a valuable transaction or a spam transaction, an authorized transaction or an unauthorized transaction, a legal transaction or an illegal transaction.
cues.zh: 因为它不为任何单一组织或机构的目标服务。它中立地遵循共识规则。每个人都中立地遵循共识规则。你的交易——没有所谓好交易或坏交易，有价值的交易或垃圾交易，授权交易或未授权交易，合法交易或非法交易。

cues.en: In these systems, there is only a valid or an invalid transaction based on the consensus rules. It doesn't matter who the sender is, who the recipient is, or what the value or asset or smart contract that is being executed is. Neutrality. Radical neutrality. And, of course, censorship resistance.
cues.zh: 在这些系统中，根据共识规则，交易只有有效或无效之分。发送者是谁、接收者是谁、执行的是什么价值、资产或智能合约，都不重要。中立性。彻底的中立性。当然，还有抗审查性。

cues.en: the ability to ensure that in order for the system to be open and borderless and transnational and Neutral it must be able to defend these properties By making it impossible for any actor or even several colluding actors from censoring disrupting blacklisting restricting seizing freezing transactions users
cues.zh: 要确保系统开放、无国界、跨国且中立，就必须能捍卫这些属性：让任何行为者，甚至多个合谋行为者，都无法审查、干扰、拉黑、限制、扣押、冻结交易或用户，也无法阻止国家参与这个网络。

cues.en: countries from participating in this network. Those are the important characteristics of these new, open, decentralized systems of trust that do not depend on institutions. What I would like to equip you with is a set of criteria to understand when you are being presented with something, perhaps to invest or to be employed or to engage in some way.
cues.zh: 这些就是新型、开放、去中心化信任系统的重要特征，它们不依赖机构。我想给你一套标准，用来判断别人向你展示某个东西时——可能是让你投资、入职或以某种方式参与——你该如何理解。

cues.en: It calls itself a blockchain or a distributed ledger or one of these other names that are coming out How can you tell? Blockchain or bullshit? They both start with a B. What's the difference? If you can replace the word blockchain with database and the brochure reads the same It's business as usual. It's not decentralized. It's not borderless neutral censorship resistant open
cues.zh: 它自称区块链、分布式账本，或者层出不穷的其他名号。怎么分辨？是区块链还是狗屁？反正都以 B 开头。区别在哪？如果你把“区块链”换成“数据库”，宣传册读起来一模一样，那就是一切照旧。它不是去中心化的，不是无国界、中立、抗审查、开放的。

cues.en: It reestablishes trust in intermediaries. It's just a database, and that is not disruptive. The idea that we're going to take this technology and use it to improve the operating margins of centralized institutions of trust, so that they can continue business as usual... I'd say it's abhorrent, but that's a strong word. It's just boring.
cues.zh: 它重新确立了对中介的信任。它只是个数据库，毫无颠覆性。说我们要拿这项技术去提高中心化信任机构的营业利润率，好让它们继续照旧运营……我想说这令人憎恶，但这词太重了。其实只是无聊。

cues.en: Really, really boring. No one got into this in order to make a few billions for a financial services clearinghouse. And if you did, I'm really sorry. That's boring. What's really exciting is the possibility of fundamentally changing the way we allocate trust on this planet, opening up the ability to collaborate.
cues.zh: 真的、真的很无聊。没人进入这个领域，是为了给一家金融服务清算机构赚几十亿美元。如果你真是为此而来，我真替你遗憾。那很无聊。真正令人兴奋的是，我们有可能从根本上改变这个星球上分配信任的方式，释放协作的能力。

cues.en: transact, engage on a global level with everyone. Simply by means of downloading an application, you can become part of a giant platform of trust that doesn't care who you are or where you came from, that doesn't require permission to participate or innovate, where a 12-year-old JavaScript programmer has the same influence as power as JPMorgan Chase. More, in fact.
cues.zh: 进行交易，在全球层面与每个人互动。只需下载一个应用，你就能加入一个巨大的信任平台：它不在乎你是谁、来自哪里，参与或创新都无需许可；在这里，一个 12 岁的 JavaScript 程序员拥有和 JPMorgan Chase 一样的影响力和权力。事实上，还更大。

cues.en: because they're doing open source and feeding into a community of collaboration that is creating a tsunami of innovation. Taking this technology and using it to strengthen the same centralized institutions so that they can improve their bottom line is boring. That is not what blockchain is. That's just the database.
cues.zh: 因为他们做开源，并反哺一个协作社区，而这个社区正在催生一场创新海啸。拿这项技术去强化同样的中心化机构，让它们改善自己的盈利，这很无聊。区块链不是这样的。那只是个数据库。

cues.en: It doesn't change anything. In fact, there are some rather disturbing possibilities in this model. Let's think about it for a second. The most commonly expressed application for these new distributed ledger technologies is to replace the function of a centralized clearinghouse with a consortium of N participants, where N is...
cues.zh: 它什么都改变不了。事实上，这种模型里有一些相当令人不安的可能性。我们稍微想一想。这些新的分布式账本技术最常见的应用，是用一个由 N 个参与者组成的联盟，来取代中心化清算机构的功能，其中 N 是……

cues.en: two, three, four, five, ten, known, permissioned, controlled participants who will assemble transactions and sign them rather than compete through market forces in a security model like Bitcoin. We discard currency as the underlying mechanism for building market-based security. We discard proof-of-work as
cues.zh: 二、三、四、五、十，已知的、需许可的、受控的参与者，他们会组装交易并签名，而不是像比特币的安全模型那样通过市场力量竞争。我们抛弃货币作为构建市场化安全的基础机制。我们抛弃工作量证明，因为它

cues.en: wasteful because all it allows you to do is decentralized, secure, and neutral censorship-resistant blockchain. We trust five named parties to sign transactions. At that point, they don't need to assemble these transactions in blocks. They can just sign the individual transactions. They don't need to chain them together. Absent proof-of-work and a system of currency incentives,
cues.zh: 很浪费，因为它所能实现的只是一个去中心化、安全、中立且抗审查的区块链。我们信任五个具名方来签署交易。到那时，他们不需要把这些交易组装成区块。他们只需签署单笔交易。他们不需要把它们串成链。在没有工作量证明和货币激励机制的情况下，

cues.en: Rewriting that is easy. There is no immutability. It is not a blockchain anymore, because there are no blocks and no chain. That is at a technical level, but let's look at the more important level. What do you achieve by replacing a clearinghouse with a consortium of players? There is something unique a clearinghouse does. If you understand the role of a clearinghouse...
cues.zh: 重写它很容易。没有不可篡改性。它不再是区块链，因为既没有区块也没有链。这是技术层面，但让我们看看更重要的层面。用一个参与者联盟取代清算所，你到底实现了什么？清算所有其独特的作用。如果你理解清算所的角色……

cues.en: One of its most important functions is that it is not a participant in the market. It has no skin in the game. The New York Stock Exchange is not an active trader. That's not an accident. That's called separation of concerns. The clearinghouse is an independent party with oversight that is not a market participant. If you take that party out...
cues.zh: 它最重要的职能之一，就是它不参与市场。它没有自身利益在其中。纽约证券交易所不是活跃交易者。这不是偶然，这叫关注点分离。清算所是一个受监督的独立方，不是市场参与者。如果把这一方拿掉……

cues.en: and replace it with five banks, all of which have skin in the game. How do you run a consensus algorithm when the incentives to cheat, front-run, manipulate the market, and break the consensus rules even adversarily against the other four parties are so high? There's no incentive to keep the consensus rules. All you're doing is you're saying, trust us. We're in a consortium. Trust us?
cues.zh: 换成五家银行，而它们全都利益相关。当作弊、抢跑、操纵市场，甚至恶意对抗其他四方、破坏共识规则的动机如此之高时，你怎么运行共识算法？根本没有遵守共识规则的动机。你所做的只是说：相信我们。我们在一个联盟里。相信我们？

cues.en: These five banks? Where were you in 2008? Where were you when Lieber was fixed? Where were you when the gold markets were fixed? Where were you when front-running and high-frequency trading was creating these monsters of crony capitalism? Trust us? Hell no. Removing the clearinghouse and replacing it with... What's the word?
cues.zh: 这五家银行？2008年你们在哪儿？Lieber 被操纵的时候，你们在哪儿？黄金市场被操纵的时候，你们在哪儿？抢先交易和高频交易制造出这些裙带资本主义怪物的时候，你们在哪儿？信任我们？去你的。移除清算所，换成……那个词怎么说？

cues.en: It's not consortium cartel. That's the word with a cartel of the same market makers who have manipulated and compromised every market in history and Doing that in a way that closes this from transparency. That's not a recipe for efficiency immutability security transparency That's not a blockchain. That's a bullshit
cues.zh: 不是联盟，是卡特尔。就是这个词——由同一批做市商组成的卡特尔，他们操纵并损害了历史上每一个市场，而且做法是把透明度关在门外。这不是效率、不可篡改、安全和透明的配方。那不是区块链。那是胡扯。

cues.en: It's a very profitable bullshit. It requires you to have confidence in the game, a con game as it's known. Be careful what you evaluate when you see these technologies. Taking something whose fundamental purpose is to remove trusted intermediaries and create an open borderless neutral system and turning it into a tool for a bunch of
cues.zh: 这是一种非常赚钱的胡扯。它需要你对这场游戏有信心——也就是人们所说的骗局。看到这些技术时，要小心你评估的是什么。把根本目的是移除可信中介、创造开放、无边界、中立系统的东西，变成一群……的工具

cues.en: untrustworthy trusted parties to manipulate markets is going to be a disaster. They are going to do it. I have some consolation in the fact that their keys will leak. When you centralize a system, you have to keep the security of those five keys. None of them have ever managed to do that. All of the companies involved in this brave new business-as-usual space...
cues.zh: 让不可信的受信任方操纵市场，将会是一场灾难。他们一定会这么干。让我稍感安慰的是，他们的密钥会泄露。当你把系统中心化时，就必须保证那五把密钥的安全。可从来没有谁做到过。所有涉足这个“勇敢新常态”业务领域的公司……

cues.en: have been hacked, breached, leaked, and whistle-blown a dozen times. They can't keep information secure. No one can. The whole point of a decentralized blockchain is you don't keep the information secure. You spread it out so thin, there's no place to attack it directly. That's what makes it secure. What happens when you concentrate it among five participants? I can't wait.
cues.zh: 已经被黑客攻击、入侵、泄露、内部举报过十几次了。他们没法保证信息安全。没人能做到。去中心化区块链的关键就在于，你不是把信息守住。你把它分散得足够薄，没有地方能被直接攻击。这才是它安全的原因。当你把它集中到五个参与者手里时，会发生什么？我等着看。

cues.en: until the anonymous WikiLeaks collaborative dump of the titans of Wall Street and their ledger of every transaction they've ever done. I can't wait. It's going to be so much fun, and it is going to happen. You cannot secure these things. So, does that mean there's nothing there? No. Again, we go back to the other side.
cues.zh: 直到匿名 WikiLeaks 协作曝光华尔街巨头，以及他们做过的每一笔交易的账本。我等不及了。那会非常有趣，而且一定会发生。你没法保护这些东西。那么，这是否意味着那里什么都没有？不。我们再次回到另一边。

cues.en: There is an incredibly promising technology and that technology is based on an architecture of openness People are examining this market and they're grasping and reaching out in darkness When you have a brand-new disruptive technology, you can't see the margins. It's like stumbling around a dark room Somewhere in there is a billion dollar company Somewhere in there is an opportunity
cues.zh: 有一项极其有前景的技术，而这项技术基于开放的架构。人们正在审视这个市场，在黑暗中摸索、伸手探寻。当你拥有一项全新的颠覆性技术时，你看不到边界。就像在黑暗房间里跌跌撞撞。那里面某处有一家十亿美元级公司，某处有一个机会。

cues.en: You have to figure out what market exists that will create opportunity, that will change the world, that will have an impact on humanity. Entrepreneurs look at other people's problems and see them as opportunities. When journalists in 1997 were writing about the imminent failure of the internet because of the impossibility of finding anything, Larry Page and Sergey Brin were finding stuff.
cues.zh: 你必须弄清楚，存在什么市场能创造机会、改变世界、对人类产生影响。创业者把别人的问题看作机会。1997年，记者们还在写互联网因无法找到任何东西而即将失败，Larry Page 和 Sergey Brin 却正在找到东西。

cues.en: multi-billion dollar empire on solving the unsolvable problem of search. There are seemingly unsolvable problems in the open, decentralized, public, transparent, neutral, censorship-resistant, global, trustless network platform that is the blockchain and these other blockchains, Bitcoin, Ethereum, and the many other systems that are gradually trying to find their niche. Where are those markets?
cues.zh: 靠解决搜索这个无解难题，建立起价值数十亿美元的商业帝国。在区块链这个开放、去中心化、公开、透明、中立、抗审查、全球化、无需信任的网络平台上，以及比特币、以太坊和其他许多正逐渐找到自身定位的系统中，都存在看似无解的问题。这些市场在哪里？

cues.en: There are three elements to success in this industry. The first one is identifying a viable market, right? You've got to stumble in the dark and find something useful. And very often, the people stumbling in the dark, they don't find anything useful. In 1997, Petco was building an online commerce empire for pet supplies. It was too early. The market didn't exist. Web grocer, web van.
cues.zh: 这个行业成功有三个要素。第一个是找到可行的市场，对吧？你必须在黑暗中摸索，找到有用的东西。而很多时候，在黑暗中摸索的人什么有用的东西都找不到。1997 年，Petco 正在打造宠物用品在线商业帝国。太早了。市场还不存在。Web grocer、Webvan。

cues.en: was delivering groceries to homes in San Francisco, failed miserably. Was that the right market? Maybe, but it was the wrong time. So that's the second important element, right? Timing. You can identify something that at some point will be enormous, but you're off by a decade. And then the most important factor, sequencing, the prerequisites. Why did Facebook not happen in 1992?
cues.zh: 当时在旧金山给各家送杂货，结果惨败。那是正确的市场吗？也许是，但时机不对。所以这就是第二个重要因素，对吧？时机。你能看出某个东西未来会非常巨大，但你可能差了十年。然后是最重要的因素：先后顺序，也就是先决条件。为什么 Facebook 没有在 1992 年出现？

cues.en: You didn't have enough density of adoption. You didn't have mobile devices that were permanently connected. You didn't even have home-based internet that was permanently on. You didn't have a dense social network in order to engage with the people you knew because the people you knew barely had email or didn't have email, right? So you can't build a system of complexity that depends on many-to-many interaction with high density.
cues.zh: 你没有足够的普及密度。你没有始终连接的移动设备。你甚至没有始终在线的家庭互联网。你没有密集的社交网络来与你认识的人互动，因为你认识的人几乎没有电子邮件，或者根本没有电子邮件，对吧？所以，你无法构建一个依赖高密度多对多交互的复杂系统。

cues.en: when you're still doing applications that are one-to-one with low density, right? It's like trying to fuse hydrogen directly into carbon. Can't do that. You've got helium, lithium, beryllium. You've got a long way to go. Keep smashing things together before you get enough density that you can start doing interesting things in organic chemistry, right? To use an example from science. Bottom line is you can't do
cues.zh: 当你还在做一对一、低密度的应用时，对吧？这就像想让氢直接聚变成碳。做不到。你得先有氦、锂、铍。你还有很长的路要走。你得不断把东西撞在一起，直到密度足够高，才能开始做有机化学里那些有趣的事，对吧？借用科学里的一个例子。归根结底，你还做不了

cues.en: advanced real estate title applications, voting on the blockchain, retail markets. You can't do consumer-to-consumer dense markets. You can't do points-of-sale retail with these systems yet. You can't do most of the things yet that might be very interesting markets. The reason you can't do them...
cues.zh: 高级房地产产权应用、区块链投票、零售市场。你没法做消费者对消费者的高密度市场。用这些系统，你还做不了销售点零售。大多数可能非常有趣的市场，你现在还做不了。你做不了它们的原因是……

cues.en: It's because there's not enough liquidity. There's not enough users. There's not enough adoption. The user interfaces are terrible. The applications are still at their infant stage. That doesn't mean these things can't happen. It just means they're not happening this year. We're going to see this play out. In order for people to have the trust to put the title of their home on this blockchain, it has to be able to secure not billions, but trillions of dollars in assets.
cues.zh: 这是因为流动性不够，用户不够，采用度也不够。用户界面很糟糕，应用还处在婴儿期。但这并不意味着这些事不可能发生，只是说今年不会发生。我们会看到它如何发展。要让人们愿意把自己房子的产权放到这条区块链上，它必须能够保障的不是数十亿、而是数万亿美元的资产。

cues.en: In order to be able to secure trillions of dollars in assets, it has to have liquidity and infrastructure. It has to have broad adoption. You're not going to get adoption on a transaction that most people do twice in their lifetime, when you can't even get them to use it for transactions they do every day. We're not going to be doing digital identity, so that everyone can have a bank account. It takes a long time until you have adequate adoption.
cues.zh: 要保障数万亿美元的资产安全，它就必须具备流动性和基础设施。它必须得到广泛采用。连人们每天都会做的交易都没法让他们使用它，你就不可能让一项大多数人一生只做两次的交易获得采用。我们不会为了让每个人都能拥有银行账户而去做数字身份。要达到足够的采用率需要很长时间。

cues.en: For the first 15 years of the internet, the application was emailed. Not until everybody had it needed it for work, did we see the second layer emerge. That created the density of adoption. Currency is the email of blockchains. Payments are the fundamental infrastructure that will enable density of adoption. It is very enticing to say,
cues.zh: 互联网的头15年，应用就是电子邮件。直到人人都拥有它、工作离不开它，我们才看到第二层浮现。这造就了采用的密度。货币就是区块链的电子邮件。支付是根本性的基础设施，将带来采用的密度。人们很容易说，

cues.en: This is about more than money. It is. Absolutely. In the long term, the vision of this technology is far beyond money. But you can't build that unless you first build the money part. That's what creates the security. That's what creates the velocity, the liquidity, the infrastructure. That's what funds the entire ecosystem. And in the end, when we do deliver, perhaps, digital identity...
cues.zh: 这不止关乎金钱。确实如此。绝对如此。长期来看，这项技术的愿景远不止于金钱。但除非你先建好“钱”这部分，否则你建不成那个愿景。正是它创造了安全性。正是它创造了速度、流动性和基础设施。正是它为整个生态系统提供资金。最终，当我们真正交付时，或许是数字身份……

cues.en: It won't be so they can open a bank account. This isn't about banking the unbanked, it is about de-banking all of us. Thank you.
cues.zh: 这不会是为了让他们能开银行账户。这不是要为没有银行账户的人提供银行服务，而是要让所有人都失去银行服务。谢谢。
